description:
FILED s446l (agent L) from a one-off gate flake, with the mechanism traced.

OBSERVED: one `tools/prove-core` run failed Pl/t/english-01.t rows 1-6 (the
first six of thirteen) and passed 7-13; the same tree passed the file three
times standalone and passed two later FULL gate runs.  Eight-way parallel
cold-cache stress of the same program (with and without the module cache)
would not reproduce it.

MECHANISM (read off the code and the live cache):
  * p-compute-cache-path keys a cached module transpile on
    sxhash(ABS-PATH | *pcl-cache-generation* | "v2") -- and p-cache-valid-p
    accepts any entry newer than the SOURCE and younger than a week.
  * Every round-5 worktree shares one ~/.pcl-cache.  A file under the
    worktree (lib/English.pm) has a per-worktree absolute path, so those keys
    cannot collide -- but a CORE module does not: /home/bernt/perl5/...
    /lib/5.40.3/Exporter.pm is ONE path for every agent.
  * The generation string is what separates two agents' entries, and an agent
    bumps it only when it makes an emission change -- AFTER it has already
    run gates and probes with a modified emitter.  During that window its
    transpiles are written at MAIN's generation, where every other agent
    reads them.
  * Measured live during s446l: ~/.pcl-cache held entries stamped gen=v2-221
    (main's, i.e. mine and anyone else's un-bumped runs) alongside v2-230
    (agent I's) and v2-235 (agent J's).  `use English` requires core
    Exporter.pm, so a poisoned Exporter entry makes every English name
    unreachable -- exactly the shape of the six failing rows -- until the
    entry is rewritten, after which later rows pass.

This is NOT a product bug: a single checkout never sees it.  It is a hazard
of the parallel-agent pattern, and it makes a FLAKE look like a regression in
whichever agent's file happens to touch the poisoned module.

OPTIONS (for the launcher/Fable to rule on, cheapest first):
  (a) key the cache path on the pl2cl/tree ROOT as well as the source path --
      one line in p-compute-cache-path, and it also fixes the same collision
      between a checkout and a worktree of a different commit;
  (b) give each agent its own cache dir (PCL_CACHE_DIR / HOME) in the launch
      instructions -- no code, but every agent must remember it;
  (c) make the launcher rule 'bump your generation string FIRST, before any
      measurement' -- but an agent with no emission change (like s446l) has no
      business bumping, so this does not cover everyone.
(a) looks right: the key already means 'this compiler's emission of this
file', and the tree root is part of which compiler.

BAR: two worktrees at the same generation with deliberately different
emission for one core module, transpiled in both -- neither may read the
other's entry; a single checkout's cache hit rate unchanged (measure a warm
gate before/after).
subject: Parallel agents SHARE ~/.pcl-cache and can poison each other's cached CORE-MODULE transpiles while their generation string is still main's -- a measurement hazard of the fan-out pattern, evidenced s446l
